title: Manneken Pis.
lines: In the heart of Brussels, in a little street close to the Grand Place, there's a tiny statue.
It's a little boy made of bronze.
He's no bigger than a cat.
And he's weeing into a little fountain!
That's Manneken Pis.
He's the most famous little man in all of Belgium.
Every day people from all over the world come to see him.
From Japan, from America, from India.
They take photos and they laugh.
But do you know why there's a weeing little boy in Brussels?
There are lots of stories about it.
Nobody knows which story is really true.
I'll tell you my favourite one.
Long, long ago Brussels was a small town, with a town wall all around it.
Bakers, blacksmiths, merchants and knights lived there.
At that time there was a war.
An enemy army was outside the town walls.
They wanted to capture Brussels.
They had a clever and nasty plan.
They wanted to blow up the town wall with gunpowder.
One dark night the enemies crept up to the wall.
They put a big pile of gunpowder against the wall.
They made a long fuse, a rope that burns.
And they lit the fuse.
Psssssss.
The little flame crept along the fuse, towards the gunpowder.
Soon the wall would explode!
But someone saw it.
A little boy.
His name was Julien.
Julien was five years old.
He couldn't sleep, and he was walking around on the town wall.
He looked down.
He saw the little flame creeping along the fuse.
What should he do?
He didn't have a bucket of water.
He didn't have time to call anyone.
The flame was almost at the gunpowder.
Then Julien had an idea.
A really crazy idea.
He really needed a wee anyway.
He stood on the edge of the wall.
He pulled down his trousers.
And he weed.
Right onto the little flame.
Psssssh!
The flame went out.
Tsss.
The fuse was wet.
The gunpowder couldn't explode anymore.
The wall was saved.
And so was the whole town!
The next morning the guards saw the wet gunpowder.
They saw the wet fuse.
And they saw the little boy, asleep on the wall.
When he woke up, Julien told them what had happened.
The people of Brussels laughed.
They laughed so hard that tears rolled down their cheeks.
But they were also very grateful.
That little boy had saved the whole town.
With a wee!
The enemies saw that their plan had failed.
They went away and never came back.
The mayor of Brussels had a little statue made.
Of Julien, exactly the way he stood there, weeing on the wall.
So that nobody would ever forget him.
And that's how Manneken Pis still stands there today.
For hundreds of years.
And do you know the funniest thing?
Manneken Pis has a whole wardrobe full of clothes!
More than a thousand outfits!
People from all over the world have made clothes for him.
There's a firefighter's outfit, a cook's, an astronaut's and a cowboy's.
There's an Indian outfit, a Japanese outfit and an African outfit.
On special days they dress him up.
At Christmas he's Father Christmas.
On Music Day he has a guitar.
And sometimes, on a very special holiday, he doesn't wee water but fruit juice!
There's also a Jeanneke Pis, a girl, and a Zinneke Pis, a little dog.
But Manneken Pis is the most famous of them all.
If you're ever in Brussels, go and see him.
He's smaller than you think.
But he was very brave.
And if you look carefully, you'll see that he's smiling a little.
The end.
